domain: Searches the four runtime action-descriptor tables by direct identifier or by the ordinal assigned to identifiers above seven.

bounded_search.reason: Rewrote both 'while (entry->id != -1) { ...; entry++; }' loops as guarded do-while ('if (entry->id != -1) { do { ...; entry++; } while (entry->id != -1); }') to force GCC's loop-rotation shape; also tried the gcc296 and old-agbcc compiler families on the resulting candidate. The rotation shape moved differing_halfwords from 70 to 65 (wrong_instructions 86 to 88, essentially a wash) but did not close the 20-byte/10-instruction size gap under any family: candidate stays 128 bytes against a 148-byte reference under routed and gcc296, and old-agbcc emits a still-shorter, unemittable-class 120-byte object.

notes: All 144 normalized core bytes are identical across the six approved GS1 editions.
The table count, 24-byte record stride, -1 terminator, and high-ID ordinal behavior come directly from the complete owner assembly. Zero DONE bytes are claimed.

Reference assembly shows each loop reads entry->id TWICE per new entry advanced to: once via ldrsh (sign-extended in one instruction) purely for the '!= -1' continuation test, and once via a separate ldrh+lsls+asrs sequence cached into a register for the NEXT iteration's value compare. The do-while respelling above matches reference's rotated control flow (guard, then post-tested body) but the compiler still CSEs the two reads of the same halfword into one instead of reproducing that double-read; this reads as a scheduler/CSE compiler-internals residual rather than a further source-shape gap, since the rotated C is already the natural idiom for the observed branch structure. Worth a permuter-style search over the loop body rather than further manual respelling.
